_about: Judgment side by side (plan 7.6b): wordings of judgment that more than one book shares, from Genesis and the prophets to the Gospels, the letters and Revelation, with what is alike and what differs. Every quotation machine-checked against the Berean; rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus from the passages the theme map cites, the Berean editors' quotation notes and a search of the whole Berean; widened by the completeness search; every Alike and Different line read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words.
columns_note: The Law & history: Genesis to Esther. Psalms & wisdom: Job to the Song of Solomon. The Prophets: Isaiah to Malachi.

rows.title: The Judge of all the earth

The Law & history: Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?
May the LORD, the Judge, decide today
Psalms & wisdom: I could only beg my Judge for mercy
I would be delivered forever from my Judge
There is surely a God who judges the earth!
Rise up, O Judge of the earth
The Prophets: the LORD is our Judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our King
Gospels & Acts: There is One who seeks it, and He is the Judge.
The letters: There is only one Lawgiver and Judge
the Judge is standing at the door!

rows.alike: Each speaks of a Judge. Some name God or the LORD as Judge: "God is a righteous judge" (Psalm 7:11), "God Himself is Judge" (Psalm 50:6), "the LORD is our Judge" (Isaiah 33:22), "God the Judge of all" (Hebrews 12:23).
rows.different: Isaiah 33:22 and James 4:12 set Judge beside lawgiver: "the LORD is our lawgiver"; "only one Lawgiver and Judge". One asks, "Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?" (Genesis 18:25); Job 9:15 has "I could only beg my Judge for mercy"; 2 Timothy 4:8 speaks of "the Lord, the righteous Judge" who will award "the crown of righteousness"; James 5:9 has "the Judge is standing at the door!"

rows.title: Coming to judge the earth; judging the world in righteousness

The Law & history: He is coming to judge the earth
Psalms & wisdom: He judges the world with justice
May he judge Your people with righteousness
Arise, O God, judge the earth
He is coming to judge the earth. He will judge the world in righteousness
He will judge the world with righteousness
The Prophets: with righteousness He will judge the poor
Gospels & Acts: I have not come to judge the world, but to save the world.
He will judge the world with justice by the Man He has appointed
The letters: how could God judge the world?
the saints will judge the world

rows.alike: "He is coming to judge the earth" is word for word in 1 Chronicles 16:33 and Psalm 96:13; "He judges the world with justice" (Psalm 9:8) and "He will judge the world with justice" (Acts 17:31); "with righteousness He will judge" (Isaiah 11:4) and "With righteousness He judges" (Revelation 19:11).
rows.different: Who judges is named differently: "God" (Psalm 82:8, Romans 3:6), "the LORD" (Psalm 96:13, 98:9), "the Man He has appointed" (Acts 17:31), "the saints" (1 Corinthians 6:2), one named only as "he", "May he judge Your people" (Psalm 72:2), and a rider "called Faithful and True" (Revelation 19:11). John 12:47 has "I have not come to judge the world, but to save the world."

rows.title: Judge the living and the dead

Gospels & Acts: the One appointed by God to judge the living and the dead
The letters: Christ Jesus, who will judge the living and the dead
Him who is ready to judge the living and the dead

rows.alike: All three have the same words: "judge the living and the dead".
rows.different: Acts 10:42 has "He commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that He is the One appointed by God"; 2 Timothy 4:1 names "Christ Jesus" and is a charge given "in the presence of God"; 1 Peter 4:5 says of others that they "will have to give an account to Him".

rows.title: The Day of the LORD, the great day

The Prophets: the Day of the LORD of Hosts will come against all the proud and lofty
the Day of the LORD is near; it will come as destruction from the Almighty
the Day of the LORD is coming-cruel, with fury and burning anger
stand in the battle on the Day of the LORD
the Day of the LORD is near. It will be a day of clouds
the Day of the LORD is near, and it will come as destruction from the Almighty
the Day of the LORD is coming; indeed, it is near
the Day of the LORD is great and very dreadful
the Day of the LORD is near in the valley of decision
Woe to you who long for the Day of the LORD!
Will not the Day of the LORD be darkness and not light
the Day of the LORD is near for all the nations
the Day of the LORD is near
On the Day of the LORD's sacrifice I will punish
The great Day of the LORD is near-near and coming quickly
a day of the LORD is coming
on the day of the LORD's feast
The letters: saved on the Day of the Lord
alleging that the Day of the Lord has already come
bound for judgment on that great day

rows.alike: The Prophets say again and again "the Day of the LORD is near" (Isaiah 13:6, Ezekiel 30:3, Joel 1:15 and 3:14, Obadiah 1:15, Zephaniah 1:7); Isaiah 13:6 and Joel 1:15 both go on, "it will come as destruction from the Almighty". The letters have "the Day of the Lord".
rows.different: Joel calls it "great and very dreadful" and Zephaniah "The great Day of the LORD"; Jude 1:6 speaks of angels "bound for judgment on that great day". Obadiah says it is near "for all the nations"; Amos warns those who "long for" it that it will be "darkness and not light"; Zephaniah 1:8 calls it "the Day of the LORD's sacrifice". In 2 Thessalonians 2:2 the readers are told not to be "easily disconcerted or alarmed" by a message "alleging that the Day of the Lord has already come".

rows.title: The day of wrath, the day of His anger

Psalms & wisdom: delivered from the day of wrath
He will crush kings in the day of His wrath
Riches are worthless in the day of wrath
The Prophets: on the day of His burning anger
He has abandoned His footstool in the day of His anger
You have slain them in the day of Your anger
In the day of the LORD's anger no one escaped or survived
Their silver and gold cannot save them in the day of the wrath of the LORD
That day will be a day of wrath
Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to deliver them on the Day of the LORD's wrath
before the Day of the LORD's anger comes upon you
Perhaps you will be sheltered on the day of the LORD's anger
The letters: you are storing up wrath against yourself for the day of wrath

rows.alike: Three say that wealth does not help in the day of wrath: "Riches are worthless in the day of wrath" (Proverbs 11:4), "Their silver and gold cannot save them" (Ezekiel 7:19), "Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to deliver them" (Zephaniah 1:18).
rows.different: Lamentations 2:21 has "You have slain them in the day of Your anger" and 2:22 "In the day of the LORD's anger no one escaped or survived". Job 21:30 says "the evil man is spared from the day of calamity"; Zephaniah 2:3 says "Perhaps you will be sheltered"; Romans 2:5 speaks to one "storing up wrath against yourself for the day of wrath, when God's righteous judgment will be revealed."

rows.title: The wrath of the LORD, the wrath of God, the coming wrath

The Law & history: great is the wrath of the LORD that burns against us
the wrath of the LORD is upon you
the wrath of the LORD has fallen upon Judah and Jerusalem
the wrath of the LORD did not come upon them
great is the wrath of the LORD that has been poured out on us
the wrath of the LORD against His people was stirred up beyond remedy
Psalms & wisdom: he who is under the wrath of the LORD will fall into it
The Prophets: By the wrath of the LORD of Hosts the land is scorched
at the wrath of the LORD of Hosts
They are full of the wrath of the LORD
Because of the wrath of the LORD, she will not be inhabited
Gospels & Acts: the wrath of God remains on him
The letters: The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven
the wrath of God is coming on the sons of disobedience
the wrath of God is coming on the sons of disobedience
Jesus our deliverer from the coming wrath
Revelation: with which the wrath of God is completed
seven golden bowls full of the wrath of God

rows.alike: "the wrath of the LORD" in the histories, Proverbs and the Prophets; "the wrath of God" in John, the letters and Revelation. Matthew 3:7 and Luke 3:7 give John's words alike, "flee from the coming wrath", and 1 Thessalonians 1:10 has "the coming wrath"; Ephesians 5:6 and Colossians 3:6 share "the wrath of God is coming on the sons of disobedience".
rows.different: The histories speak of it on Judah and Jerusalem ("has fallen upon Judah and Jerusalem"; "did not come upon them during the days of Hezekiah"), Jeremiah 50:13 of Babylon. Romans 1:18 says it "is being revealed from heaven", John 3:36 that it "remains on him" who "rejects the Son", Revelation 15:1 that with the seven plagues it "is completed".

rows.title: Who can stand before Him?

The Law & history: Who can stand in the presence of the LORD, this holy God?
no one can stand against You
no one can stand before You
Who can stand up to the sons of Anak?
no one can stand against you
Psalms & wisdom: who is able to stand against Me?
When You are angry, who can stand before You?
If You, O LORD, kept track of iniquities, then who, O Lord, could stand?
Who can withstand His icy blast?
The Prophets: Who can withstand His indignation? Who can endure His burning anger?
who can endure the day of His coming? And who can stand when He appears?

rows.alike: The same kind of question, who can stand or who can endure, is asked about the LORD or His day: 1 Samuel 6:20, Psalm 76:7, Psalm 130:3, Joel 2:11, Nahum 1:6, Malachi 3:2. 2 Chronicles 20:6 and Ezra 9:15 say "no one can stand".
rows.different: The occasion differs: the men of Beth-shemesh ask it of "this holy God"; Psalm 76:7 "When You are angry"; Psalm 130:3 if He "kept track of iniquities"; Joel of "the Day of the LORD"; Malachi of "the day of His coming". Ezra says it "before You in our guilt"; Job 41:10 has the question in the first person: "who is able to stand against Me?"

rows.title: Weighed on the scales

Psalms & wisdom: let God weigh me with honest scales
Weighed on the scale, they go up
his motives are weighed out by the LORD
does not He who weighs hearts consider it?
If only my grief could be weighed
The Prophets: you have been weighed on the scales and found deficient
weighed the mountains on a scale

rows.alike: What is weighed: "actions" (1 Samuel 2:3), "motives" (Proverbs 16:2), "the heart" (Proverbs 21:2), "hearts" (Proverbs 24:12). "The LORD" weighs in Proverbs 16:2 and 21:2, "God" in Job 31:6; Job 31:6 and Daniel 5:27 speak of "scales".
rows.different: Proverbs 16:2 and 21:2 set the LORD's weighing against how a man's ways look to himself: "pure in his own eyes"; "seem right to him". Job asks to be weighed "with honest scales, that He may know my integrity"; Daniel 5:27 reads "you have been weighed on the scales and found deficient"; Psalm 62:9 says men weighed "go up", "but a vapor".

rows.title: Every hidden thing brought to light

Psalms & wisdom: God will bring every deed into judgment, along with every hidden thing, whether good or evil
for all these things God will bring you to judgment
our secret sins in the light of Your presence
The Prophets: They are not hidden from My face
Gospels & Acts: There is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.
there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed
there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed
The letters: He will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and will expose the motives of men's hearts
Nothing in all creation is hidden from God's sight

rows.alike: "every hidden thing" (Ecclesiastes 12:14), "our secret sins" (Psalm 90:8), "not hidden from My face" (Jeremiah 16:17), "nothing hidden" (Luke 12:2), "men's secrets" (Romans 2:16), "what is hidden in darkness" (1 Corinthians 4:5), "Nothing in all creation is hidden" (Hebrews 4:13).
rows.different: Ecclesiastes 12:14 says "every deed", "whether good or evil"; 1 Corinthians 4:5 adds "At that time each will receive his praise from God"; Romans 2:16 says God will judge men's secrets "through Christ Jesus, as proclaimed by my gospel"; Psalm 90:8 has "You have set our iniquities before You, our secret sins in the light of Your presence". Mark 4:22 and Luke 8:17, shown for the shared words, both have "there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed".

rows.title: Before the judgment seat; giving an account

Psalms & wisdom: I would give account of all my steps
Gospels & Acts: men will give an account on the day of judgment for every careless word they have spoken
Pilate was sitting on the judgment seat
brought him before the judgment seat
he drove them away from the judgment seat
in front of the judgment seat
he sat on the judgment seat
I am standing before the judgment seat of Caesar
I sat on the judgment seat
The letters: we will all stand before God's judgment seat
each of us will give an account of himself to God
we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive his due for the things done in the body, whether good or bad
Him to whom we must give account
as those who must give an account
they will have to give an account to Him

rows.alike: "we will all stand before God's judgment seat" (Romans 14:10) and "we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ" (2 Corinthians 5:10); an account is given in Job 31:37 ("give account"), Hebrews 4:13 ("give account"), Matthew 12:36, Romans 14:12, Hebrews 13:17 and 1 Peter 4:5 ("give an account").
rows.different: Romans 14:10 says "God's judgment seat", 2 Corinthians 5:10 "the judgment seat of Christ". What is spoken of: "every careless word" (Matthew 12:36), "the things done in the body, whether good or bad" (2 Corinthians 5:10), "himself" (Romans 14:12), "all my steps" (Job 31:37), and in Hebrews 13:17 leaders who "watch over your souls". In the other Gospel and Acts verses the judgment seat is Pilate's, Gallio's, Festus's and Caesar's.

rows.title: Do not judge

The Law & history: you are to judge your neighbor fairly
Gospels & Acts: Do not judge, or you will be judged.
with the same judgment you pronounce, you will be judged
Do not judge, and you will not be judged.
The letters: on whatever grounds you judge the other, you are condemning yourself
Who are you to judge someone else's servant?
Why, then, do you judge your brother?
let us stop judging one another
judge nothing before the appointed time
Anyone who speaks against his brother or judges him speaks against the law
who are you to judge your neighbor?
so that you will not be judged

rows.alike: "Do not judge" (Matthew 7:1, Luke 6:37); "Who are you to judge" (Romans 14:4) and "who are you to judge your neighbor?" (James 4:12); "let us stop judging one another" (Romans 14:13). Matthew 7:1 and Luke 6:37 join it to being judged: "or you will be judged", "and you will not be judged". James 5:9 has "so that you will not be judged" after "Do not complain about one another".
rows.different: Leviticus 19:15, of not perverting justice, commands "you are to judge your neighbor fairly"; James 4:12 asks "who are you to judge your neighbor?" after "There is only one Lawgiver and Judge". 1 Corinthians 4:5 says "before the appointed time" and "wait until the Lord comes"; Romans 2:1 says "you who pass judgment do the same things".

rows.title: The righteous and the wicked: judged, distinguished, separated

The Law & history: Will You really sweep away the righteous with the wicked?
so that the righteous and the wicked are treated alike
Psalms & wisdom: the wicked will not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous
God will judge the righteous and the wicked
The Prophets: I will judge between one sheep and another, between the rams and the goats
I Myself will judge between the fat sheep and the lean sheep
I will judge between one sheep and another
you will again distinguish between the righteous and the wicked
Gospels & Acts: The angels will come and separate the wicked from the righteous
He will separate the people one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats

rows.alike: "the righteous" and "the wicked" set apart: "God will judge the righteous and the wicked" (Ecclesiastes 3:17), "distinguish between the righteous and the wicked" (Malachi 3:18), "separate the wicked from the righteous" (Matthew 13:49). Ezekiel 34:17 and Matthew 25:32 both have sheep and goats: "between the rams and the goats"; "separates the sheep from the goats".
rows.different: In Genesis Abraham asks it as a question, against the two being "treated alike". In Ezekiel the Lord GOD judges within "My flock", "between the fat sheep and the lean sheep"; Malachi 3:18 adds "between those who serve God and those who do not"; in Matthew 13:49 "The angels" separate "at the end of the age", and in Matthew 25:32 He separates "the people".

rows.title: All the nations gathered for judgment

The Prophets: I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will enter into judgment against them
there I will sit down to judge all the nations on every side
My decision is to gather nations, to assemble kingdoms, to pour out upon them My indignation
Gospels & Acts: He will sit on His glorious throne
All the nations will be gathered before Him

rows.alike: "I will gather all the nations" and "sit down to judge all the nations" (Joel 3:2, 3:12); "to gather nations" (Zephaniah 3:8); "He will sit on His glorious throne" and "All the nations will be gathered before Him" (Matthew 25:31-32).
rows.different: Joel names a place, "the Valley of Jehoshaphat", and a cause, "concerning My people, My inheritance, Israel"; Zephaniah 3:8 says "to pour out upon them My indignation-all My burning anger". In Matthew it is "the Son of Man" who sits, "and all the angels with Him".

rows.title: Coming with His holy ones, with His angels

The Law & history: came with myriads of holy ones, with flaming fire at His right hand
The Prophets: the LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones with Him
Gospels & Acts: the Son of Man will come in His Father's glory with His angels
When the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the angels with Him
when He comes in His Father's glory with the holy angels
when He comes in His glory and in the glory of the Father and of the holy angels
The letters: at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all His saints
when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with His mighty angels
the Lord is coming with myriads of His holy ones

rows.alike: In each, the one who comes has others with Him: "with myriads of holy ones" (Deuteronomy 33:2) and "with myriads of His holy ones" (Jude 1:14); "all the holy ones with Him" (Zechariah 14:5) and "all the angels with Him" (Matthew 25:31); "with His angels" (Matthew 16:27), "with the holy angels" (Mark 8:38).
rows.different: Deuteronomy 33:2 says "The LORD came from Sinai"; Zechariah 14:5 says "the LORD my God will come" and Jude 1:14 "the Lord is coming". Those with Him are named differently: "holy ones" (Deuteronomy 33:2, Zechariah 14:5, Jude 1:14), "angels" (Matthew 16:27, 25:31, 2 Thessalonians 1:7), "saints" (1 Thessalonians 3:13). The one who comes is "the LORD my God" (Zechariah 14:5), "the Son of Man" (Matthew 16:27, 25:31), "our Lord Jesus" (1 Thessalonians 3:13), "the Lord Jesus" (2 Thessalonians 1:7), and "the Lord" in the words Jude gives from Enoch, "the seventh from Adam".

rows.title: A consuming fire

The Law & history: the glory of the LORD was like a consuming fire on the mountaintop
the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God
the LORD your God goes across ahead of you as a consuming fire
consuming fire came from His mouth
Psalms & wisdom: consuming fire came from His mouth
The Prophets: His tongue is like a consuming fire
with a flame of consuming fire
Who of us can dwell with a consuming fire?
The letters: For our God is a consuming fire.

rows.alike: "the LORD your God is a consuming fire" (Deuteronomy 4:24) and "our God is a consuming fire" (Hebrews 12:29); 2 Samuel 22:9 and Psalm 18:8 are word for word: "consuming fire came from His mouth".
rows.different: In Exodus 24:17 it is how "the glory of the LORD" looked "in the eyes of the Israelites"; in Deuteronomy 9:3 the LORD "goes across ahead of you as a consuming fire"; Isaiah 30:27 says "His tongue is like a consuming fire"; Isaiah 33:14 gives the question to "The sinners in Zion": "Who of us can dwell with a consuming fire?"

rows.title: Fire of His anger and jealousy

The Law & history: a fire has been kindled by My anger
Psalms & wisdom: In His wrath the LORD will engulf them, and the fire will consume them
Fire goes before Him and consumes His foes on every side
The Prophets: The fire set for Your enemies will consume them!
the LORD will come with fire
My anger will kindle a fire that will burn against you
like a flaming fire that consumes everything around it
The whole earth will be consumed by the fire of His jealousy
all the earth will be consumed by the fire of My jealousy
The letters: raging fire that will consume all adversaries

rows.alike: "The fire set for Your enemies will consume them!" (Isaiah 26:11), "consumes His foes" (Psalm 97:3), "raging fire that will consume all adversaries" (Hebrews 10:27); Zephaniah 1:18 and 3:8, "consumed by the fire of His jealousy" and "of My jealousy"; Deuteronomy 32:22 and Jeremiah 15:14, a fire kindled by "My anger".
rows.different: In Lamentations 2:3 He "has burned in Jacob like a flaming fire that consumes everything around it"; Jeremiah 15:14 has "My anger will kindle a fire that will burn against you" after "I will enslave you to your enemies"; Isaiah 26:11 has "but they do not see it" before "The fire set for Your enemies will consume them!"; Zephaniah 1:18 says "The whole earth"; 2 Thessalonians 1:8 says the vengeance is "on those who do not know God and do not obey the gospel".

rows.title: Eternal fire, everlasting flames

The Prophets: Who of us can dwell with everlasting flames?
Gospels & Acts: be thrown into the eternal fire
into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels

rows.alike: "the eternal fire" in Matthew 18:8 and 25:41, and "eternal fire" in Jude 1:7; Isaiah 33:14 has "everlasting flames".
rows.different: Isaiah 33:14 is the question of "The sinners in Zion"; Matthew 18:8 sets it against "to enter life crippled or lame"; Matthew 25:41 says it is "prepared for the devil and his angels"; Jude 1:7 says "Sodom and Gomorrah" are "on display as an example".

rows.title: Thrown into the furnace, the fire, the lake of fire

Psalms & wisdom: You will place them in a fiery furnace at the time of Your appearing
may they be thrown into the fire
The Prophets: its body was destroyed and thrown into the blazing fire
the day is coming, burning like a furnace
thrown into the blazing fiery furnace
thrown into the blazing fiery furnace
thrown at once into the blazing fiery furnace
deliver us from the blazing fiery furnace
throw them into the blazing fiery furnace
they were thrown into the blazing fiery furnace
fell into the blazing fiery furnace
the door of the blazing fiery furnace
Gospels & Acts: they will throw them into the fiery furnace
throw them into the fiery furnace
be thrown into the fire of hell
be thrown into the eternal fire
Revelation: Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire
he was thrown into the lake of fire

rows.alike: "a fiery furnace" (Psalm 21:9) and "the fiery furnace" (Matthew 13:42, 13:50); "thrown into the blazing fire" (Daniel 7:11), "thrown into the fire of hell" (Matthew 18:9), "thrown into the eternal fire" (Matthew 18:8), "thrown into the lake of fire" (Revelation 20:14, 20:15).
rows.different: What is thrown differs: "its body" (Daniel 7:11), "Death and Hades" (Revelation 20:14), anyone "not written in the Book of Life" (Revelation 20:15). Malachi 4:1 says the day itself is "burning like a furnace". In Daniel 3 the "blazing fiery furnace" is for "whoever does not fall down and worship" (3:6).

rows.title: Cut down and thrown into the fire

The Prophets: they will cut down the choicest of your cedars and throw them into the fire
it is cast into the fire for fuel
Like the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel
Gospels & Acts: every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire
Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire
Such branches are gathered up, thrown into the fire, and burned.

rows.alike: Matthew 3:10 and Luke 3:9 are word for word, and Matthew 7:19 nearly so: a tree without good fruit is "cut down and thrown into the fire"; Jeremiah 22:7 has "cut down" and "throw them into the fire". Ezekiel 15:6 speaks of "the wood of the vine" given "to the fire for fuel", and John 15:6 of branches "thrown into the fire".
rows.different: Matthew 3:10 and Luke 3:9 begin "The axe lies ready at the root of the trees"; Matthew 7:19 does not. Ezekiel 15:6 goes on, "so I will give up the people of Jerusalem"; John 15:6 says it of one who "does not remain in Me"; Jeremiah 22:7 says "your cedars".

rows.title: Like chaff before the wind, like stubble before the fire

Psalms & wisdom: like chaff swept away by a storm?
they are like chaff driven off by the wind
May they be like chaff in the wind
The Prophets: as a tongue of fire consumes the straw
driven before the wind like chaff on the hills
the multitude of the ruthless like blowing chaff
a whirlwind sweeps them away like stubble
to windblown chaff with his bow
Surely they are like stubble; the fire will burn them up.
became like chaff on the threshing floor in summer
like chaff blown from a threshing floor
like the crackling of fire consuming stubble
the house of Esau will be stubble
like stubble that is fully dry
Gospels & Acts: He will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire
He will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire

rows.alike: "like chaff" with "the wind" (Psalm 1:4, 35:5, 83:13; Isaiah 17:13); "like stubble" (Exodus 15:7, Isaiah 47:14) and "will be stubble" (Malachi 4:1), each beside burning or fire ("Your burning wrath"; "the fire will burn them up"; "I will set them ablaze"). Matthew 3:12 and Luke 3:17 have the same sentence word for word: "He will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire".
rows.different: Psalm 35:5 and 83:13 pray it ("May they be like chaff"; "Make them like tumbleweed"); Exodus 15:7 says what was done ("it consumed them like stubble"); in Daniel 2:35 "the iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold" became "like chaff"; in Isaiah 41:15 "you" are made a threshing sledge to "reduce the hills to chaff". Matthew has the wheat gathered "into the barn", Luke "into His barn".

rows.title: Weeping and gnashing of teeth; the outer darkness

Psalms & wisdom: he will gnash his teeth and waste away
He gnashes His teeth at me
they gnashed their teeth at me
The Prophets: They hiss and gnash their teeth
Gospels & Acts: thrown into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth
where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth
where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth
throw him into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth
assign him a place with the hypocrites, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth
throw that worthless servant into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth
There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth
they gnashed their teeth at him

rows.alike: "where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth" six times in Matthew, and "There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth" in Luke 13:28; Psalm 112:10 says the wicked man "will gnash his teeth". Matthew 8:12, 22:13 and 25:30 all have "the outer darkness".
rows.different: Matthew sets it with "the outer darkness" three times and "the fiery furnace" twice (13:42, 13:50); Luke 13:28 with seeing "Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God". Psalm 112:10 says "The wicked man will see and be grieved". Elsewhere teeth are gnashed "at" someone: "at me" (Job 16:9, Psalm 35:16), "at them" (Psalm 37:12), "at him" (Acts 7:54).

rows.title: The day of vengeance

Psalms & wisdom: he will show no mercy in the day of vengeance
The Prophets: the LORD has a day of vengeance, a year of recompense
the day of our God's vengeance
the day of vengeance was in My heart
a day of vengeance against His foes
